title: Config-change eval harness for latency vs quality tradeoffs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: build a repeatable, automated evaluation harness that ties configuration and model-variant changes to both latency SLOs and response quality metrics. This ticket scopes the infra and methodology for measuring latency-quality tradeoffs caused by batching and KV-cache related config flips (microbatch size, batch windows, cache TTL, cache bypass heuristics, and tokenization-affecting changes).

Scope and deliverables:
- A YAML-driven experiment definition that enumerates config axes (microbatch sizes 1,2,4,8,16; batch windows 10ms/20ms/50ms; KV cache TTLs 0/30s/2m; bypass_pct 0/1/5/10) and model variants (fp16, int8-quant, fp16+flash-attn kernels).
- A canonical prompt set representing production distributions: chat prompts (30%), instruction-fulfill (40%), code-completion (20%), long-context summarization (10%). Each prompt has expected output fingerprints (gold/approx) and automatic scoring hooks.
- Metrics collected per-experiment: token-level p50/p95 latency, cold-start percent, throughput (tokens/sec), mean quality score (nlg-embed-sim & task-specific metrics), hallucination rate, and delta vs baseline.
- A regression alert rule config: fail if quality drops >2% absolute on weighted-suite or if latency regression causes p95 to exceed SLA by >20% without quality improvement.
- An evaluation report template (CSV + visual tradeoff curve) and a PR checklist for config/model changes that includes a link to the generated report and suggested rollback thresholds.

Methodology notes:
- Use production-sampled token length distribution to drive synthetic runners; supplement with a 2000-sample live query set for human-checked quality verification.
- Use embedding-based similarity (dense-sim) for bulk quality scoring, with a small stratified human eval on any candidate that shows >1% gap to baseline.
- Control for non-determinism by seeding RNGs, running 3 independent trials, and reporting mean and stdev.

Infrastructure integration:
- Harness runs on dedicated infra with isolated GPU pool; results are stored in the evaluations bucket and linked to the PR.
- Console: add a per-experiment dashboard tile showing latency-quality frontier and per-config heatmap.

Acceptance criteria summary:
- CI job that can run a defined experiment matrix and emit a single-line status pass/fail.
- Tradeoff curve visualization in Console for the top 6 configs.
- A documented PR checklist entry that requires attaching the experiment report for any runtime config or model-variant change with non-trivial expected cost or latency impact.

Risks and open questions:
- How to weight quality across task types (we propose 0.4 chat, 0.35 instruction, 0.15 code, 0.1 long-context).
- The right human sampling size for borderline cases (proposal: 100 judgments per flagged config).
- Incorporating tokenization-induced KV cache behavior changes: may need tokenizer-agnostic fingerprinting.
